I have written Go in 3 public repositories, from 2014 to 2022.

What it was for: [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (1), [Systems and infrastructure](@/projects/systems.md) (1) and [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (1).

Most recently: [rest-hello-world-benchmark](@/work/rest-hello-world-benchmark.md): Benchmark of Hello World REST Endpoint in various languages / frameworks; [docker-datasciencetoolbox](@/work/docker-datasciencetoolbox.md): Dockerized http://datasciencetoolbox.org; [apollo-box](@/work/apollo-box.md): All needed data science stuff in one box.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses Go: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links Go to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
